session.question: What are biomasses converted into through thermochemical decomposition?
session.answer: Biomasses are converted through thermochemical decomposition into bio-oils, syngas, hydrogen (H2), biofuels, heat, and biochar. Biochar is specifically described as a carbon-free fertiliser. (rout2022sustainablevalorisationof chunk 1)
session.raw_answer: Biomasses are converted through thermochemical decomposition into bio-oils, syngas, hydrogen (H2), biofuels, heat, and biochar. Biochar is specifically described as a carbon-free fertiliser. (pqac-4c140292)
session.context:
pqac-ac7f379d: The excerpt explains that bio-oils are produced via the decomposition of biomass through thermochemical conversion. These bio-oils are described as renewable liquid fuels and as sustainable resources that can be used to produce epoxy resins. The thermochemical processing techniques mentioned include organic solvent liquefaction, fast pyrolysis, and hydrothermal liquefaction.
From Philip Agbo, Abhijeet Mali, Dongyang Deng, and Lifeng Zhang. Bio-oil-based epoxy resins from thermochemical processing of sustainable resources: a short review. Journal of Composites Science, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/jcs7090374, doi:10.3390/jcs7090374.

pqac-37754ea6: The excerpt explains that lignocellulosic biomass is thermochemically converted into value-added chemicals and biofuels, especially bio-oil. It notes that bio-oil is a major product of biomass conversion but has drawbacks such as instability, low heating value, corrosivity, and high viscosity, which is why upgrading methods are needed. The paper focuses on thermochemical conversion of lignocellulosic biomass into mass-producible fuels and discusses emerging methods for improving bio-oil quality, along with sustainability and environmental impacts.
From Wujun Liu and Han‐Qing Yu. Thermochemical conversion of lignocellulosic biomass into mass-producible fuels: emerging technology progress and environmental sustainability evaluation. ACS Environmental Au, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1021/acsenvironau.1c00025, doi:10.1021/acsenvironau.1c00025.

pqac-4c140292: The excerpt discusses thermochemical conversion technologies for animal manures and states that these processes can generate several useful products. Specifically, biomasses/manures converted through thermochemical decomposition can produce bio-oils, syngas, hydrogen (H2), biofuels, heat, and biochar, with biochar described as a carbon-free fertiliser. The review also notes that these technologies are used for manure management and valorisation, aiming at energy and nutrient recovery.
From Prangya Ranjan Rout, Daya Shankar Pandey, Macsen Haynes-Parry, Caitlin Briggs, Helmer Luís Cachicolo Manuel, Reddicherla Umapathi, Sanjay Mukherjee, Sagarika Panigrahi, and Mukesh Goel. Sustainable valorisation of animal manures via thermochemical conversion technologies: an inclusive review on recent trends. Waste and Biomass Valorization, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1007/s12649-022-01916-5, doi:10.1007/s12649-022-01916-5.

pqac-6c07d94c: The excerpt describes thermochemical techniques as methods for converting diverse waste materials, including biomass, into valuable products such as chemicals and fuels. It mentions key processes like pyrolysis, gasification, and liquefaction, which are evaluated for energy efficiency, product yield, product quality, and environmental impact. The overall goal is waste-to-value conversion and sustainable resource recovery within a circular economy context.
From Halil Durak. Comprehensive assessment of thermochemical processes for sustainable waste management and resource recovery. Processes, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/pr11072092, doi:10.3390/pr11072092.

pqac-02b1d594: The excerpt describes a review of biomass-to-sustainable hydrogen production routes, including thermochemical, biological, and electrochemical approaches. It states that biomass is used as a raw material for hydrogen production and discusses thermochemical decomposition as one of the patented approaches for producing H2 from biomass. The abstract emphasizes optimizing parameters and evaluating operational challenges for scalable hydrogen generation from biomass within a circular economy context.
From M.G. Eloffy, Ahmed M. Elgarahy, Ayman N. Saber, Ahmed Hammad, Dina M. El‐Sherif, M. Shehata, Ahmed Mohsen, and Khalid Z. Elwakeel. Biomass-to-sustainable biohydrogen: insights into the production routes, and technical challenges. Chemical Engineering Journal Advances, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ceja.2022.100410, doi:10.1016/j.ceja.2022.100410.

Question: What are biomasses converted into through thermochemical decomposition?
